active_themes.label: Warsh's Credibility Trap Tightens
active_themes.summary: Warsh has now lost all intellectual cover for rate cuts. The data is stagflationary: 4.2% inflation, zero wage growth, zero spending growth. His only path to market credibility is a public statement that rate hikes remain on the table. Until then, the market will correctly assume policy error—a Fed chairman cutting rates into inflation.

active_themes.label: Iran Escalation Pauses—Window Closing
active_themes.summary: Iran signaled an 'end to military operations' after the US launched strikes, giving markets a 72-hour window for either de-escalation deal or negotiation collapse. Oil has retreated, providing temporary relief. The window closes in 3-7 days. Until then, energy prices remain the binding constraint on inflation expectations and Fed policy.

active_themes.label: Lenders Silent Through Jobs Report
active_themes.summary: Discover, Capital One, and Amex had maximum cover today to announce deposit rate cuts or consumer credit tightening—flat May spending, stagflationary backdrop, Hammack's dominance over Fed policy. They remained silent, which on its surface is surprising. This silence will not hold beyond 3-7 days. The institutional delay is now the narrowest open window in the repricing chain. When the first major lender moves, it will be a cascading signal: credit is tightening, demand is weakening, and equities are mispriced for that reality.

active_themes.label: Soft Landing Dead—Repricing Pending
active_themes.summary: May's 0% MoM spending combined with 4.2% inflation and stagnant wages removes all remaining soft-landing credibility. Equities have not repriced into a stagflation scenario where the Fed cannot cut aggressively without validating higher inflation expectations. The repricing begins when the first major lender (Discover, Capital One, Amex) announces credit tightening, expected within 3-7 days.

active_themes.label: Yields Stuck at Stagflation Range
active_themes.summary: 10-year remains 3.9-4.1%; 30-year at 2007 highs. Hammack's warning and today's spending data validate stagflation scenario. Yields will not move lower without hard demand destruction (not evident) or inflation rollover (not happening). This is the correct price for an economy cutting rates while inflation stays elevated.

active_themes.label: Bond Market Vindication Accelerates
active_themes.summary: The bond market correctly priced stagflation since May 15 (10-year 3.9-4.1%, 30-year at 2007 highs). Today's 4.2% CPI confirms the thesis empirically. Equities have been slow to reprice—the S&P is still trading at levels that assume either a soft landing (now dead) or imminent rate cuts (inconsistent with 4.2% inflation and Warsh's public caution). The repricing acceleration depends on institutional credit action within 3-7 days.

active_themes.label: Institutional Silence at Inflection
active_themes.summary: Major lenders had perfect cover today to cut deposit rates or announce credit tightening—stagflationary backdrop, flat spending, Warsh's policy error. All three remained silent. This silence will break in 3-7 days as credit tightening becomes unavoidable. When it does, it will cascade: equities will reprice into demand destruction and margin compression.

open_watchlist.condition: First major lender (Discover, Capital One, Amex) publicly announces deposit rate cuts or consumer credit tightening
open_watchlist.meaning: This is the trigger for equity repricing; expect 1-3% decline in the following 1-3 days, with full repricing of 3-5% over 3-5 days.

open_watchlist.condition: Iran-US negotiations officially collapse or US publicly walks away from talks
open_watchlist.meaning: Oil targets $95+ within 48 hours; stagflation narrative reinforces; Warsh loses geopolitical cover and faces rate-hike pressure from markets.

open_watchlist.condition: Capital One, Discover, or American Express publicly announces deposit rate cuts or consumer credit tightening
open_watchlist.meaning: This is the signal that institutional credit is tightening in response to stagflation. Equities will reprice down 3–5% over the following 2–3 weeks once this happens.

open_watchlist.condition: US-Iran nuclear deal officially announced or US officially walks away from negotiations
open_watchlist.meaning: If a deal materializes, Warsh gets 2-3 weeks of breathing room and oil rolls back, reducing near-term energy inflation pressure. If negotiations collapse, oil targets $95 and Warsh loses his final policy escape valve.

open_watchlist.condition: Warsh or another Fed official publicly states that rate hikes remain on the table through 2027
open_watchlist.meaning: This would be a public reversal from the implied message of May and would restore some credibility to the Fed's stagflation management. Without this statement, markets will assume policy error and keep repricing equities downward.

open_watchlist.condition: US-Iran nuclear deal officially announced or US publicly walks away from negotiations
open_watchlist.meaning: If deal: oil stays under $80, repricing pauses briefly, Warsh gets tactical air but stagflation remains unsolved. If collapse: oil spikes toward $95, equities fall another 2-3%.

open_watchlist.condition: 10-year Treasury yield breaks above 4.1% or 30-year breaks below 2007 highs
open_watchlist.meaning: The bond market is signaling either inflation acceleration or a demand shock; either way, equities face structural headwinds.

open_watchlist.condition: Warsh or another Fed official publicly states rate hikes remain on the table through 2027
open_watchlist.meaning: This is policy capitulation and confirms Hammack's dominance. It removes the assumption of policy error and stabilizes bond yields, but it also confirms stagflation is the base case.

open_watchlist.condition: Major lender (Discover, Capital One, Amex) publicly announces deposit rate cuts or tightens consumer credit standards
open_watchlist.meaning: This is the cascade trigger: the market will read it as confirmation that demand is rolling over and the Fed is wrong to cut, forcing a 3-5% equity repricing downward.

open_watchlist.condition: US and Iran announce a formal nuclear deal or US officially walks away from negotiations
open_watchlist.meaning: A deal brings energy relief (equities rally 2-3%), a collapse keeps inflation elevated (equities fall 2-3% on stagflation extension).
